title: Stackable parts tray with lid
prompt: Stackable parts tray with a lid, printed as separate pieces. Tray: 100 x 60 mm outside, 1.6 mm walls, 2 mm floor, rim 28 mm above the very bottom. Under the floor there's a 3 mm tall stacking foot: a rectangular ring with 1.6 mm walls that fits inside the tray below with 0.3 mm clearance all round, so 96.2 x 56.2 mm outside, centred under the tray. Inside, one 1.6 mm divider across the width at the middle makes two equal compartments; it stops 3 mm below the rim so the foot of the tray above clears it. The lid is a 100 x 60 x 2 mm plate with the same ring as the foot on top, so it drops into a tray (flip it over to use it). Tray corner at the origin with the foot on Z = 0, and put the lid 10 mm to the right (+X) of the tray, also on Z = 0.

hidden_tests.description: Evaluates cleanly and every body is a valid closed solid
Foot, floor, walls, divider, lid plate and lid ring are solids (touching bodies: IR v0 has no booleans)
Side-by-side layout: 210 x 60 mm footprint, 28 mm tall
Tray corner at the origin, everything on Z = 0
The tray walls: a 100 x 60 mm body reaching the 28 mm rim
Foot and lid ring are the same 96.2 x 56.2 x 3 mm ring with 1.6 mm walls (0.3 mm clearance in the 96.8 x 56.8 opening)
The foot is centred under the tray (1.9 mm in from the outside) and sits on Z = 0
One 1.6 mm divider across the width at X = 50, spanning the inside, its top 3 mm below the rim (Z = 25)
The lid plate: 100 x 60 x 2 mm, 10 mm to the right of the tray
Total volume ≈ 40222.7 mm³ ±1% (checks wall, floor, divider and ring thickness)

notes: Foot/ring 477.44·3 = 1432.32 each, floor 12000, walls 501.76·23 = 11540.48, divider 1.6·56.8·20 = 1817.6, lid plate 12000. Walls may also be modelled from Z = 3 with the floor inside them: same volume.
